conceptPrimer.heading: Back-EMF and the Motor KVL
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: A DC motor's rotating armature generates back-EMF $E_b = \frac{\Phi Z N P}{60 A} \propto \Phi N$ ($P$ poles, $Z$ conductors, $A$ parallel paths). Motor KVL: $V = E_b + I_a R_a$ (a generator writes $E_g = V + I_a R_a$ — the sign is the tell). $E_b$ self-regulates: $I_a = \frac{V - E_b}{R_a}$; at standstill $N = 0 \Rightarrow E_b = 0$, so starting current is huge — hence the 3-point/4-point STARTER. Micro-check: $V = 240\ \text{V}$, $R_a = 0.5\ \Omega$, $I_a = 30\ \text{A}$: $E_b = 240 - 15 = 225\ \text{V}$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Lap vs Wave Winding and Torque
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: LAP winding: $A = P$ paths — high current, low voltage (thick conductors). WAVE winding: $A = 2$ — high voltage, low current. Electromagnetic torque $T_a = \frac{E_b I_a}{\omega} \propto \Phi I_a$, and speed obeys $N \propto \frac{V - I_a R_a}{\Phi}$: weaken the flux and the motor speeds UP (flux loss is a runaway hazard for shunt machines too). Micro-check: at constant power $E_b I_a$, halving $\Phi$ roughly doubles $N$.

conceptPrimer.heading: DC Shunt Motor: the Constant-Speed Workhorse
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Shunt field $\Phi \approx$ constant, so $T_a \propto I_a$ (linear) and speed barely falls from no-load to full load — ideal for LATHES and machine tools. Field-weakening control pushes speed above base speed; accidentally losing shunt-field excitation makes $\Phi \to 0$ and $N \to \infty$: dangerous overspeed. Micro-check: torque doubling from $10\ \text{N·m}$ to $20\ \text{N·m}$ roughly doubles $I_a$ (linear law).

conceptPrimer.heading: DC Series Motor: Traction Torque, Runaway Risk
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Series field carries $I_f = I_a$, so before saturation $\Phi \propto I_a$ and $T_a \propto I_a^2$ — enormous starting torque for TRACTION, cranes and hoists. The same law is fatal at no-load: $I_a \to 0 \Rightarrow \Phi \to 0 \Rightarrow N \to \infty$ (runaway) — a series motor MUST NEVER start unloaded. After saturation $T \propto I_a$ (linear region). Micro-check: doubling $I_a$ (unsaturated) multiplies torque four-fold.

conceptPrimer.heading: Synchronous Speed, Slip and Rotor Frequency
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: A $P$-pole stator fed at $f$ Hz sweeps the field around at $N_s = \frac{120f}{P}$ rpm. An induction motor runs below it at slip $s = \frac{N_s - N}{N_s}$ ($s = 1$ at standstill, $0.02$–$0.05$ at full load), and rotor currents oscillate at $f_r = sf$. Micro-check: $N_s = 1500$, $N = 1440$: $s = 0.04$, $f_r = 2\ \text{Hz}$ — the rotor 'sees' 2 Hz, not 50 Hz.

conceptPrimer.heading: Air-Gap Power Split and the 1-φ Capacitor Start
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Air-gap power divides $P_{\text{ag}} : P_{\text{rcu}} : P_m = 1 : s : (1-s)$ — rotor copper loss is exactly $s\,P_{\text{ag}}$, which is why low slip means high efficiency. A single-phase winding produces only a PULSATING field: zero starting torque, NOT self-starting. Ceiling fans and pumps add an auxiliary winding in series with a phase-splitting CAPACITOR, creating a second field in quadrature — the start of a rotating field. Micro-check: $P_{\text{ag}} = 1000\ \text{W}$ at $s = 0.04$: rotor copper loss $40\ \text{W}$, mechanical $960\ \text{W}$.

memoryHooks: Motor $V = E_b + I_aR_a$; generator $E_g = V + I_aR_a$ — sign is the species.
Shunt: torque linear, speed flat — the lathe motor.
Series: torque squared, traction, but never naked (no-load runaway).
Air-gap pie: $1 : s : (1-s)$ — rotor loses exactly $s$ of it.
Field weakened, speed up — flux is the brake.
One winding pulsates; the capacitor's twin makes it turn.
Starter exists because $E_b$ takes time to wake up.
commonMistakes: Writing generator KVL for a motor (or vice versa).
Using $A = P$ for wave windings (it's lap; wave is $A = 2$).
Claiming a series motor is safe at no-load.
Interpolating shunt speed linearly in $I_a$ instead of in $E_b$.
Saying $f_r = f$ at full load (it is $sf$, a few Hz).
Assigning rotor copper loss as $(1-s)P_{\text{ag}}$ (that's mechanical power).
Forgetting the capacitor in single-phase start discussions.
examChecklist: Fix the KVL sign: motor $V = E_b + I_aR_a$.
Compute $E_b$ first in every DC-motor speed problem; ratio speeds via $E_b$ at constant $\Phi$.
Choose lap ($A = P$, current) vs wave ($A = 2$, voltage) by service.
Quote torque laws: shunt linear, series squared (unsaturated).
Never allow a series motor to run unloaded.
Compute $N_s = 120f/P$, slip, and $f_r = sf$ in one breath.
Split air-gap power $1 : s : (1-s)$ and read rotor loss as $sP_{\text{ag}}$.
